title: Runtime LTS regression gates and SLOs (patch releases)
author: Sean Gallagher
body:
## Purpose
This page defines the **reliability and performance gates** required to ship a **Runtime LTS patch release** (e.g., `runtime-1.20-lts.3`). The intent is to provide enterprise customers a slower-change channel with predictable risk, while keeping the patch process auditable and consistent.

This document is **normative** for LTS patch promotion. If a gate is overridden, the override must be explicitly documented in the release notes and the audit evidence bundle.

**Applies to:** runtime kernel + scheduling artifacts shipped under the Runtime LTS channel (Hosted, Dedicated, and Private-compatible artifacts).

**Owners:**
- Primary: **SRE** (Sean Gallagher; Rafael Mendes)
- Perf signals: **Observability/Perf** (Allison Grant)
- Release execution: **Release Eng** (Connor O'Brien; Sahana Iyer)
- Runtime sign-off: **Runtime** (Noah Patel / delegate)

---

## Definitions
**RC (Release Candidate):** a candidate build of an LTS patch version that has passed required CI and is ready for canary.

**Canary:** limited rollout of the RC to a constrained subset of production traffic/capacity with enhanced monitoring.

**Baseline:** the performance and stability reference point. For LTS patches, baseline is:
1) the **previous LTS patch release** in the same LTS line (e.g., baseline for `1.20-lts.3` is `1.20-lts.2`), and
2) the current **LTS benchmark baseline set** published in Benchmark Lab.

**Key metrics (runtime-facing):**
- **TTFT**: time-to-first-token
- **TPOT**: time per output token (or derived tokens/sec)
- **p95/p99 latency**: tail latency percentiles on standard workloads
- **OOM rate**: fraction of requests failing due to out-of-memory
- **Server 5xx rate**: runtime-originated failures

---

## Release quality bar (LTS-specific)
LTS patches must prioritize **stability** over novelty.

A patch must meet all of:
- No new customer-facing behavior changes unless explicitly declared and approved as a backport exception.
- No regression beyond the thresholds in the tables below on the standard perf suites.
- Canary must run for the minimum duration and stay within the error budget and tail-latency constraints.

If a patch contains both security and non-security fixes, it must meet the same gates; security urgency does **not** waive core runtime stability requirements without an explicit override.

---

## SLOs and regression thresholds
### 1) Production canary SLOs (Hosted + Dedicated canaries)
These are evaluated during the canary window on the canary fleet(s). Thresholds are relative to the baseline LTS patch.

| Category | Metric | Gate (must be true for full canary window) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Availability | Runtime-originated 5xx rate | **≤ baseline + 0.03% absolute** AND **≤ 0.10% absolute** | Uses request-level classification (exclude customer 4xx and upstream timeouts not attributable to runtime). |
| Correctness | Crash/restart rate (runtime pods) | **≤ baseline + 10%** | Restarts include OOMKills and fatal exits. |
| Correctness | OOM rate | **≤ baseline + 0.01% absolute** AND **≤ 0.05% absolute** | Must also show no sustained GPU memory leak trend (see “Leak watch”). |
| Latency | p95 end-to-end latency | **≤ baseline + 3%** | Evaluated per primary route/model group. |
| Latency | p99 end-to-end latency | **≤ baseline + 5%** | Tail gate; any sustained breach is treated as a release blocker. |
| Streaming | TTFT p95 | **≤ baseline + 5%** | Streaming workloads are especially sensitive to scheduler changes. |
| Throughput | Tokens/sec (aggregate) | **≥ baseline - 2%** | Computed on like-for-like capacity. |

**Leak watch (required):** for the duration of the canary, GPU memory usage at steady load must not show a monotonic upward trend that implies a leak. SRE uses the “GPU residency / KV cache / fragmentation” dashboards; any suspected leak blocks promotion until explained.

### 2) Offline perf suite gates (Perf Canary + Benchmark Lab)
These gates are evaluated pre-canary and may be re-run after fixes.

| Suite | Workload coverage | Gate vs baseline | Required for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `perf-canary/lts-latency` | chat + completion; short and long context; streaming on/off | p95 **≤ +2%**, p99 **≤ +4%** | All patches |
| `perf-canary/lts-throughput` | batching sensitivity; concurrency sweep | throughput **≥ -1%** | All patches |
| `benchmark-lab/lts-baseline` | standardized prompt sets; stable dataset/versioning | no single test worse than **+5% p99** | All patches |

**Interpretation rule:**
- One outlier run does not automatically fail the patch; however, promotion requires either (a) a rerun that passes, or (b) a documented explanation with SRE approval that the outlier is noise and not reproducible.

### 3) Error budget policy for LTS canaries
We treat the canary window as a “mini error budget” for the candidate.

**Canary error budget (pass criteria):**
- Total runtime-originated errors (5xx + runtime timeouts attributable to runtime) must stay within the gates in the SLO table above.
- Additionally, the canary must not trigger **SEV2+** incident criteria attributable to the RC.

**If a canary hits any rollback trigger (see below), the canary budget is considered exhausted and promotion is blocked.**

---

## Canary requirements
### Canary scope
LTS patches must canary in at least one production-like environment.

**Default canary scope (normal patches):**
- Hosted: 1 canary cell per region (or the smallest unit we can safely isolate)
- Dedicated: at least one internal dedicated pool (Redwood-owned) + one low-risk customer-approved pool when available

**Private (VPC/on-prem):** does not canary automatically. For LTS patches that materially affect Private stability (scheduler/memory), Release Eng must coordinate a **Private upgrade rehearsal** per the Private LTS upgrade/rollback guide.

### Canary duration
| Patch type | Minimum canary duration | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Normal LTS patch | **24 hours** | Must include at least one daily peak period for the primary region. |
| Perf-sensitive patch (scheduler, batching, KV cache) | **48 hours** | Or until we see stable tails under peak. |
| Security-only emergency patch | **6 hours** | Must still meet rollback triggers and core SLO gates unless explicitly waived. |

### Canary monitoring checklist (must be attached to release evidence)
- [ ] p95/p99 latency by route + model group
- [ ] TTFT p95 for streaming endpoints
- [ ] runtime 5xx by error class (OOM, invalid state, kernel error, scheduler timeout)
- [ ] GPU memory (allocated, reserved, fragmentation proxy) and leak watch
- [ ] Tokens/sec and queueing time
- [ ] Pod restarts / OOMKills
- [ ] Customer-impact signals: support tickets tagged runtime, on-call pages attributable to runtime

---

## Rollback triggers (hard)
If any trigger occurs during canary, SRE should initiate rollback immediately and block promotion pending investigation.

### Immediate rollback triggers
Rollback now if any of the following are observed and attributable to the RC:
1) **Runtime-originated 5xx rate ≥ 0.20% absolute for 10 minutes** (rolling window) in any canary cell.
2) **p99 latency regression ≥ +15% for 15 minutes** (rolling window) for a primary route/model group.
3) **Crash loop / restart storm**: restart rate ≥ 2x baseline for 10 minutes, or any sustained OOMKill pattern.
4) **Data integrity/correctness incident**: misrouting, corrupted outputs, broken streaming protocol, or deterministic correctness failure tied to kernels.
5) **SEV2+ incident** declared with the RC as a suspected cause.

### Conditional rollback triggers (requires SRE judgment, but defaults to rollback)
1) **OOM rate > 0.05% absolute** sustained for 30 minutes.
2) **Throughput regression ≥ -5%** sustained for 30 minutes at comparable utilization.
3) Reproducible **GPU memory leak** signature.

**Decision authority:** The on-call SRE (primary) has authority to rollback. Notify Release Eng + Runtime owner immediately in `#eng-releases` and `#eng-oncall`.

---

## Release gating workflow (what must be true to promote)
Promotion from RC → final LTS patch requires the following evidence.

### A) Pre-RC (required)
- All required CI checks green (see CI/provenance doc).
- Offline perf suite gates passed (or approved exception).
- Backport risk tier documented in the release notes draft.

### B) RC creation (required)
- RC artifacts signed and attestations generated.
- RC tagged with commit SHAs and build provenance.

### C) Canary (required)
- Canary executed for minimum duration.
- Canary SLO gates met for full duration.
- No rollback triggers fired.

### D) Final promotion (required)
- Runtime owner sign-off (Noah Patel or delegate).
- SRE sign-off (Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes; for after-hours, on-call SRE).
- Release Eng sign-off (Connor O’Brien).
- Release notes include: “Risk level”, “Perf deltas summary”, “Known issues/mitigations”, and explicit mention of any waived gates.

---

## Exception process (rare)
If a patch cannot meet a gate but is needed (e.g., high-severity security fix), the following is required:
- Document which gate(s) are waived and why.
- Add mitigations and a rollback plan to the release notes.
- Obtain explicit approvals from:
  - SRE owner (Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes)
  - Release Eng lead (Connor O’Brien)
  - Runtime org sign-off (Noah Patel)
  - Security reviewer (Marcus Lin) if security-related
- For enterprise customer-impacting exceptions: Product (Lauren Bishop or Vivek Kulkarni) must approve customer messaging.

---

## Operational notes for patch engineers
### How to attribute failures to the RC (avoid false rollback)
- Confirm error class is runtime-originated (not upstream gateway timeouts or customer-side cancellations).
- Compare against baseline cell(s) still running previous LTS patch.
- Check if a single model family is responsible (e.g., only long-context requests).

### Known “noisy” signals (do not use alone)
- Single-node GPU ECC spikes without corroborating runtime errors
- One-off benchmark outliers without reproduction
- Traffic mix shifts (must normalize by workload tag)

---

## Change log
- 2026-02-12: Tightened offline suite p95/p99 gates and added TTFT p95 gate for streaming.
- 2026-01-08: Added explicit emergency security canary duration guidance and exception approval list.
- 2025-12-10: Initial publication for Runtime LTS pilot.
